task.title: CATEGORYDELETE
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

A merchant deleted an old "Summer sale" category, and every product that was only in that category disappeared from the shop: the products are gone, carts that held them stopped working, and orders that included them can no longer be opened. Opening the deleted category by its id now shows a server error rather than "not found".

Deleting a category (DELETE /api/v1/private/category/{id}) must delete only the category and the categories below it:

- Its products are kept, with their stock, price and any other categories. They are just no longer in the deleted categories: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} doesn't list those categories any more.
- Carts and orders that hold its products are unaffected: they read, change and check out exactly as before.
- Categories below the deleted one are deleted with it, and their products are kept in the same way.
- A deleted category gives HTTP 404 Not Found from GET /api/v1/category/{id}, isn't in GET /api/v1/category, and listing its products (GET /api/v1/products?category={id}) lists none.
- Deleting a category that doesn't exist gives HTTP 404 Not Found.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: The added API test covers only an empty category and does not exercise descendant categories, products, product v2 responses, carts, orders, or checkout. No independently inspectable CI checks exist.
findings.impact: The task's central guarantees that products, stock, carts, and orders survive deletion remain unverified; a regression in those flows could pass.
findings.correction: Add and run end-to-end tests creating products in deleted and retained categories, then verify v2 product data, cart read/change/checkout, existing order access, descendant cleanup, category listing, product filtering, and both 404 cases.

findings.problem: Deletion removes PRODUCT_CATEGORY rows but does not remove CatalogCategoryEntry rows that reference the categories. CatalogCategoryEntry has a required CATEGORY_ID association without a delete cascade.
findings.impact: Deleting a category used in a catalog can fail on the database foreign key, so the required DELETE operation is not reliable for all existing categories.
findings.correction: Remove catalog-entry associations for the entire category subtree before deleting categories, or define and verify an appropriate cascade, with regression coverage.

findings.problem: The friendly-url route was narrowed to values beginning with a letter and containing only letters, digits, and hyphens.
findings.impact: Existing friendly URLs beginning with a digit or containing valid previously accepted characters such as underscores or dots no longer match any route, creating an unrelated API regression.
findings.correction: Disambiguate numeric IDs from friendly URLs without imposing this narrower format, for example by excluding only an all-numeric segment from the friendly-url pattern.

runs.report:
## Repository confirmation

This checkout is Shopizer and contains the requested API, service, model, repository, and integration-test modules. No GitHub issue or label catalog was supplied.

## Evidence

- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/catalog/category/CategoryServiceImpl.java:231-285` gathers the target category and descendants, finds their products, then deletes products with one affected category. For products with multiple categories it removes affected associations, but the emptiness check uses the stale `product` instance at lines 270-272.
- `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/catalog/product/Product.java:103-120` defines the owning `PRODUCT_CATEGORY` many-to-many association, so deletion should remove only affected category links from the product and persist the product.
- `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/catalog/category/Category.java:60-65` defines child categories with `CascadeType.REMOVE`; deleting the root category is intended to remove descendants.
- `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/shoppingcart/ShoppingCartItem.java:59-65,89-91` stores product identity/SKU and keeps the product reference transient.
- `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/order/orderproduct/OrderProduct.java:34-49` stores order-product SKU/name/quantity rather than a category relationship. Keeping the product row is therefore required for existing cart/order behavior.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/facade/category/CategoryFacadeImpl.java:244-265` raises `ResourceNotFoundException` for a missing category GET, while `:360-368` resolves deletion through the generic `categoryService.getById(categoryId)` proxy instead of the store-scoped nullable lookup. This should be changed so a nonexistent ID deterministically produces HTTP 404.
- `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/category/CategoryManagementAPIIntegrationTest.java:335-341` has only a legacy delete smoke test against `/services/DEFAULT/category/100` and asserts nothing. `sm-core/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/catalog/CategoryTest.java:24-61` only creates and cleans up a category.

## Problem and scope

The current deletion implementation conflates category cleanup with product deletion. It must retain every product, remove only links to the deleted category subtree, and then delete the category subtree. The deletion lookup must also use the merchant-scoped category lookup so missing IDs return 404 rather than an ORM/proxy error. No cart/order schema or behavior change is indicated.

## Recommended implementation

1. In `CategoryServiceImpl.delete`, retain the existing subtree discovery and category deletion flow, but for every affected product remove only the intersection of its categories with the collected category IDs/categories, persist the updated product once, and never call `productService.delete`.
2. Ensure deletion of the root category removes descendants and their descriptions through the existing category cascade, while product links are removed before category rows are deleted.
3. In `CategoryFacadeImpl.deleteCategory(Long, MerchantStore)`, use the existing store-scoped `categoryService.getById(categoryId, store.getId())` and throw `ResourceNotFoundException` when it returns null. Preserve store authorization behavior.
4. Add regression coverage at service/API level for a product only in the deleted category, a product in both deleted and retained categories, products in descendants, cart access/change/checkout, existing orders, deleted-category GET/list/product filtering, and deletion of an unknown ID.

## Acceptance checks

- DELETE `/api/v1/private/category/{id}` retains all affected product rows, stock, price, SKU, variants, and other fields.
- Product details no longer contain deleted category IDs but retain unaffected categories.
- Products assigned only to deleted categories remain retrievable and usable in carts and existing orders.
- Descendant categories are deleted and their product links are removed without deleting products.
- GET `/api/v1/category/{deletedId}` returns 404; the category hierarchy omits it; `/api/v1/products?category={deletedId}` returns no products.
- DELETE of an unknown category ID returns 404 and does not alter other data.
- Existing category deletion behavior and authorization remain intact.

## Likely affected components

- `sm-core/.../catalog/category/CategoryServiceImpl.java`
- `sm-shop/.../facade/category/CategoryFacadeImpl.java`
- `sm-core` category/product tests
- `sm-shop` category/product/cart/order integration tests

## Complexity and assumptions

Moderate: the core fix is localized, but end-to-end regression coverage spans persistence and cart/order flows. It is an evidence-based assumption that the current category cascade is retained and that no migration is needed; the mappings and stored cart/order snapshots support that approach. No explicit design approval is needed; route directly to Implement.
runs.summary: Completed triage; no production files were changed. The deletion bug is localized and can proceed directly to implementation with regression tests.

A merchant deleted an old "Summer sale" category, and every product that was only in that category disappeared from the shop: the products are gone, carts that held them stopped working, and orders that included them can no longer be opened. Opening the deleted category by its id now shows a server error rather than "not found".

Deleting a category (DELETE /api/v1/private/category/{id}) must delete only the category and the categories below it:

- Its products are kept, with their stock, price and any other categories. They are just no longer in the deleted categories: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} doesn't list those categories any more.
- Carts and orders that hold its products are unaffected: they read, change and check out exactly as before.
- Categories below the deleted one are deleted with it, and their products are kept in the same way.
- A deleted category gives HTTP 404 Not Found from GET /api/v1/category/{id}, isn't in GET /api/v1/category, and listing its products (GET /api/v1/products?category={id}) lists none.
- Deleting a category that doesn't exist gives HTTP 404 Not Found.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.
</task>
